prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
competitors_mentioned: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR)
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right one depends on your neighborhood, system type, urgency, budget and whether you want a one‑time repair or a long‑term service plan. That said, here’s how to find the best AC repair company in Houston and a few well‑reviewed options to start with.

If you want me to pull nearby providers, tell me your ZIP or neighborhood and whether you need emergency service.

Quick shortlist (well‑known, commonly recommended in Houston)
- John Moore Services — long‑established, local company with broad HVAC experience and good local reviews.
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (local franchise) — national franchise with 24/7 emergency service and many technicians.
- One Hour Heating & Air / Benjamin Franklin (franchise brands) — fast response times, service guarantees.
- Aire Serv / local reputable independents — some independent shops have excellent reputations and lower prices; check reviews.

How to pick the best one
- Verify license/registration: Texas requires HVAC contractors to register with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR). Ask for their TDLR registration number and confirm it online.
- Check reviews: Google, Yelp, Angi, and BBB. Look for recent reviews about repairs similar to yours.
- Certifications: NATE-certified technicians are a plus.
- Written estimate: Get a clear written estimate with parts, labor, taxes, warranty, and any fees.
- Warranty: Ask about parts and labor warranties and whether manufacturer warranties remain valid after repair.
- Emergency availability: Does the company offer 24/7 emergency repairs if you need it?
- Transparency & communication: Good companies will diagnose first, explain options (repair vs replacement), and avoid high‑pressure sales.
- Price vs value: Extremely low bids can be a red flag. Compare 2–3 estimates.

Questions to ask a tech when they arrive
- Are you licensed and insured? Can I see your TDLR number and proof of insurance?
- Do you have NATE or manufacturer certifications for my system?
- What is the diagnosis and recommended fix? What are other options?
- How long will the repair take and do you guarantee the work?
- Is there a diagnostic fee if I decline the repair?
- Will replacing parts affect my manufacturer warranty?

Typical price ranges (rough ballpark)
- Service call/diagnostic: $75–$150 (sometimes credited toward repair)
- Minor repairs (capacitor, fan motor start/run capacitor, contactor): $150–$500
- Major components (compressor, coil): $800–$3,000+
(Prices vary by system, brand and accessibility.)

If you tell me your ZIP code, the make/model of your system and whether it’s an emergency, I can find top‑rated local HVAC companies and recent reviews for your area.
